title: Intrinsic kinetic graph Poincare stress for Q3 likelihood rows
question: Can the R-399 conditional shell use the Hamiltonian kinetic carre-du-champ directly, by replacing the unstable coordinate nearest-neighbour comparison with the intrinsic Poincare gap of its momentum-weighted graph?
method: For each positive conditional law pi, build the symmetric momentum conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi) in the q basis.
Compute the first positive eigenvalue of the pi-weighted graph Laplacian and test the exact graph identity E_kin(f)=f^T L f together with E_kin(f)>=gap(pi) Var_pi(f) on every actual likelihood row.
Repeat the full R-403 cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and orientation grid, while recording the intrinsic gap profile separately from the coordinate form.
Use a p-to-q mutation as a hostile structural test: q is diagonal in the q basis and must produce zero graph edges, unlike the genuine momentum graph.
Rebuild the finite model in an independent lane and compile the scalar nonnegativity skeleton in Lean.
finding: The primary lane passes 1398/1398 assertions over 7 volume-two systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; 15840 rows have variance above the declared floor and 5280 are constant-row diagnostics.  The independent lane passes 1388/1388, the hostile lane 6/6, the integrated verifier 37/37 and Lean R404 compiles.  The generalized momentum-weighted graph gap ranges from 0.7570174175402339 to 5.647863075935321 and remains positive at every declared cutoff; the minimum profile rises from 0.7570174175402339 at d=3 to 2.4233910464474144 at d=12.
decision_reason: R-403 showed that the coordinate-form upper ratio cannot be treated as a cutoff-independent constant.  R-404 removes that unstable comparison at finite level and confirms an exact intrinsic graph representation of the kinetic form with a positive finite conditional Poincare gap across the same stress grid.  This advances a route-local interface, but the finite eigenvalue profile is not an analytic cutoff-independent lower bound and does not close any QFT or common-core gate.

adversarial_review.check: The commutator trace and graph quadratic form are computed independently and compared row by row.
The conditional law is used as the mass matrix, the constant mode is checked at zero and disconnected/nonfinite graphs fail.
Rows below the variance floor are counted but not used for ratios; the Poincare residual remains checked on every row.
A non-importing lane rebuilds the oscillator model, Gibbs states, histories, conditional rows and spectrum within 5e-5.
Replacing p by diagonal q yields zero edges while the genuine graph has positive gaps on the selected baseline and late rows.
Finite positivity is not promoted to cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion uniformity, a common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

next_action: Prove an analytic lower bound for the momentum-weighted conditional graph gap on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian common core, with source, phase, volume and exhaustion uniformity; then transfer that intrinsic form to the R-399 shell without reintroducing the unstable coordinate upper comparison.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite intrinsic kinetic graph Poincare stress only.  It proves no cutoff-independent or volume-independent gap, no common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The positive finite graph gap shows that an intrinsic-form route is viable on the declared ladder, not that a uniform lower bound exists in the regulator or thermodynamic limit.
